How your writing looks on the label and on tape titles: pen, or a typewriter.
Live wallpaper: the whole deck as your background. The reels spin while recording or playing.
Widgets: new-tape counter, REC status (tap to record), or both side by side.
Location not allowed, so tapes won\'t get a place.
Lock REC on: tap REC on the deck (or tap Vol-Down three times quickly) and it keeps recording until you tap it once more. Long sessions are cut into one-hour tapes.
Snap your fingers while recording to flag the moment. The FLAG key does the same. Jump between flags when playing the tape in the deck.
When REC is locked on, silence is left off the tape. Each cut keeps a short gap so you can hear where it was. Holding REC always records everything.
Sensitivity: HIGH starts on quieter sounds (whispers, a far-off voice); LOW needs louder sound and ignores more background noise.
Note the place in each tape\'s info (coordinates and a place name). Stays on the phone, but goes inside the file when you send a tape.
AUTO lets the phone choose. A plugged-in, USB or Bluetooth mic is remembered and used whenever it\'s connected; without it, the phone\'s own mic records.
The chosen mic isn\'t connected right now.

Hold the play/pause button on wired earphones for a second to lock REC on; hold again to stop. A short press while recording flags the moment; otherwise it goes to your music as usual. Needs the volume-key trigger below switched on. Some Bluetooth headsets may not pass the button through.

Deletes deck tapes you\'ve already heard after this many days. Kept: unheard tapes, tapes with a title or flags, the tape in the deck, and everything on the shelf or in the vault. %1$s days before, the deck shows a warning and the tapes are marked ✂ in the list.
Key clicks when recording starts and stops. Uses the media volume.
A very faint tape hiss while recording, just for the feel. Kept low enough that the mic barely hears it (a bit louder in headphones, where it can\'t leak onto the tape).
Shows the REC indicator, and a \"new tapes\" reminder on the lock screen for the morning.

Tap Vol-Down, then press & HOLD it again → records while held, release to stop. Or tap it three times quickly to lock REC on; then one tap stops it. Works with the screen on or on the lock screen. Enable \"Dic2Phone volume-key trigger\" under Installed apps / Downloaded apps.
Pick Dic2Phone as Default digital assistant app. Then Pixel squeeze (Active Edge) or the assistant gesture starts a recording; tap the screen, press a volume key or the power button to stop.
Settings → Advanced features → Side button → Double press → Open app → \"Quick REC\". Double-pressing the side key then starts recording right away.
Adds a \"%1$s\" tile to the pull-down shade.
Let Dic2Phone run unrestricted so the triggers still work after a night in standby.
NATURAL keeps voices at their own pitch at any speed. TAPE works like a real deck: faster sounds higher, slower sounds deeper.
Jump over long quiet stretches (over a second) while playing. The tape itself isn\'t changed.
Hold REW / FF to wind the tape like a real deck, motor whirr and all (a tap still skips 10 s). Adds a CUE key to the deck: lit, you hear the tape as it winds.
Make a tape sound like it came off an old portable recorder. Your recordings stay clean: when you SEND a tape you can pick WITH TAPE SOUND, and the effects are baked into the copy that\'s sent.
Cheap-tape hiss and a faint transport-motor whine.
Dull, narrow tone: worn head, small mic.
Slight pitch wobble from an uneven capstan.
Soft tape compression: loud bits squashed, quiet bits lifted.
Also hear tapes through the effects when playing them in the app.

Each tape is given its effects once and the copy is kept, so it plays with effects straight away. Missing ones are made while the phone is left idle (not on battery saver). Android clears them by itself if storage runs low.

Dic2Phone turns your phone into a pocket dictaphone that looks, sounds and feels like an old cassette recorder (or a MiniDisc). Hold REC to catch a thought, a meeting or a tune, then play it back with flags, captions and tape effects. Your recordings stay on your phone unless you share them.

Free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version. It comes with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY. The key sounds are not part of this license: see KEY SOUNDS below.

Dic2Phone collects nothing. No account, no ads, no analytics, no telemetry, no crash reports: nothing about you or your recordings is ever sent to the developer or to anyone else. The app works fully offline. It only goes online when you download a caption model (from Hugging Face). If you turn on WHERE RECORDED, the place name is looked up by your phone\'s own geocoder (usually a Google service), and the place is saved only in the tape on your phone.

Dic2Phone was designed, directed and tested by WolfyD, and much of its code was written with an AI coding assistant (Claude, by Anthropic). Every change was tried on a real phone, but like any software it can have bugs: reports are welcome on GitHub.\n\nInside the app, AI is used only for captions: OpenAI\'s Whisper speech model, running on your phone. Your recordings are never sent anywhere to be transcribed.

The deck\'s key clicks and cassette sounds are real recordings from Pixabay, trimmed and filtered for this app. They are used under the Pixabay Content License: they are NOT covered by the app\'s GPL license and may not be extracted or reused on their own. They are not in the public source code; builds from source use simple synthesized clicks instead.

Select tapes and press TEXT (or TRANSCRIBE on the deck) to turn speech into text: subtitles while playing, a transcript to read or send, .srt files, and search across all tapes. It all runs on the phone; only the speech model is downloaded, once.
Not available: this phone isn\'t 64-bit ARM.
AUTO guesses per tape. Picking the language is more reliable for short tapes.

Transcribe new tapes by themselves: right after recording, or later when the phone has been left alone for a while (screen off, unused, usually overnight). WHEN IDLE works best with Battery set to unrestricted (REC tab).

The vault needs a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) on this phone. Set one up, then come back.

Tapes in here are encrypted on this phone and only play after your fingerprint or screen-lock PIN. Leaving the app locks it again.\n\nCareful: if you ever remove the phone\'s screen lock, the key is destroyed and the tapes in the vault are lost for good. They\'re not in backups either.
